const t = $json;
return [{ json: { record_id: t.record_id, status: 'invalid', failure_type: 'transform', reasons: [t.transform_error], record: t.record, batch_id: t.batch_id } }];

nodes.name: Check Circuit Breaker
nodes.notes: Breaker state lives in an external service (Redis-backed) so it's shared across every record in the batch and across concurrent batches, not just this one item's execution.

parameters.jsCode:
const t = $json;
return [{ json: { record_id: t.record_id, status: 'skipped', failure_type: 'circuit_open', reasons: ['downstream destination circuit breaker is open; skipped to avoid piling onto an active outage'], record: t.transformed, batch_id: t.batch_id } }];

nodes.name: Load to Destination
nodes.notes: fullResponse:true is required to read statusCode downstream -- with neverError alone you only get the parsed body, not the status.

parameters.jsCode:
const t = $json;
return [{ json: { record_id: t.record_id, status: 'loaded', reasons: [], record: t.transformed, batch_id: t.batch_id } }];

nodes.name: Build Success Outcome
nodes.notes: Runs on the original merged item, not on the output of Record Breaker Failure -- fired in parallel with it, not chained after it, so this branch never loses record/transformed fields.

nodes.name: Record Breaker Failure
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget side effect, run in parallel with Build Load Failed Outcome off the same source item -- not chained before it, so this call's own response never overwrites the record's fields.

parameters.jsCode:
const t = $json;
return [{ json: { record_id: t.record_id, status: 'load_failed', failure_type: 'load', reasons: [`destination returned status ${t.statusCode}`], record: t.transformed, batch_id: t.batch_id } }];

nodes.name: Log to Dead Letter Store
nodes.notes: Durable audit trail for every non-loaded record. Terminal side-effect branch -- deliberately not chained back into the aggregate, since a dead-letter store outage should never affect the batch summary response.

nodes.name: Operational Failures Present?
nodes.notes: Distinguishes bad source data (invalid -> just logged) from system/destination trouble (load_failed/skipped -> pages ops via Slack). Invalid-only batches don't page anyone.

parameters.name: text
parameters.value: ={{ 'Batch ' + $json.batch_id + ' had operational failures: ' + $json.counts.load_failed + ' load_failed, ' + $json.counts.skipped + ' skipped (of ' + $json.counts.total + ' total).' }}
